teach.heading: Contracts change the money, not the structure.
teach.body: Your entry can be clean and your stop loss can be correct, but if your size is too big, the trade becomes emotionally heavy. Position sizing is what makes the same setup feel manageable or reckless — the chart doesn't care how many contracts you're in, but you will.
teach.dayliNote: Keep your size consistent. Going heavier because confidence is high, or doubling size after a loss, is emotion talking — not a risk plan.

experience.intro: Walk the same setup through a streak of wins, then a loss.

steps.prompt: Two traders take the identical setup — same entry, same stop, same target — but one uses 1 contract and the other uses 10. Is one trade objectively better structured?

options.label: No — the structure is identical; only the dollar risk and emotional weight differ
options.feedback: Right — sizing changes the weight of the trade, not its quality.

options.label: Yes — more contracts always means a better trade
options.feedback: More contracts doesn't make a setup better — it only makes it bigger.

steps.prompt: You just had two wins in a row and feel great. Do you increase your size because confidence is high?

options.label: No — size should come from your risk plan, not your mood
options.feedback: Right — confidence isn't a risk management input.

options.label: Yes — you've earned bigger size
options.feedback: Sizing up because of a feeling, not a plan, is exactly how good runs turn into big losses.

steps.prompt: After a loss, a trader doubles her next position size to "win it back faster." What's actually happening here?

options.label: Emotion is driving her sizing decision, not her risk plan
options.feedback: Exactly — that's revenge sizing, and it compounds risk right when discipline matters most.

options.label: That's a smart way to recover losses quickly
options.feedback: Increasing size to chase back a loss usually increases risk at the worst possible moment.

reinforce.question: Two traders take the identical setup — same entry, same stop, same target — but one uses 1 contract and the other uses 10. Is one trade objectively better structured than the other?
options: No — the structure is identical; only the dollar risk and emotional weight differ between them
Yes — more contracts always means a better trade
Yes — fewer contracts always means a safer, more valid setup

reinforce.question: Explain why the same chart setup can be a smart trade for one trader and a reckless trade for another.
reinforce.modelAnswer: The setup itself — entry, stop, target — is identical for both, but position size determines how much dollar risk and emotional weight is actually attached to it. The same structurally sound setup can be reasonable at a small size and reckless at an oversized position, because sizing decides how much is actually on the line, not the chart.
